title: THE BIAS OF HARMFUL LABEL ASSOCIATIONS IN VISION-LANGUAGE MODELS

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring the frequency and confidence of zero-shot Vision-Language Models (VLMs) predicting harmful labels (e.g., non-human primates, pigs, cockroaches) for human face crops across different apparent skin tones (using Fitzpatrick and Monk scales) from the Casual Conversations datasets.
Comparing the proportion of harmful zero-shot label associations made by VLMs across self-identified gender categories (cis men, cis women, and non-binary/transgender individuals).
Evaluating the disparity in harmful label predictions across self-identified age buckets (young adult, adult, middle-age adult, and old adult).
Analyzing how the presence of physical adornments (e.g., face masks, glasses, makeup, beards/mustaches, hair covers) impacts the frequency of harmful label associations.
